name: Topic 36: Hydration timing across a workday
defaultTargetFormula: No separate target; uses Topic 30 drinks target (male 2500 ml, female 2000 ml, est.) distributed over the day: about 12% on waking, 35-40% before lunch, about 40% from afternoon to early evening, 10-15% with dinner, little after 21:00 (FitPlate design, est.). Slot size 200-300 ml, never prompt more than 500 ml at once. ICMR-NIN 2020 water values Not found; timing evidence is weak.

drinks.name: Plain water
drinks.notes: Best on waking, between meals, before lunch (optional preload), with dinner sips

drinks.name: Chai (milk tea, up to 2 tsp sugar)
drinks.notes: est.; 120 ml; mid-morning or 17:00; keep 1 h away from meals if iron-deficient; caffeine 30-65 mg (secondary); not within about 5 h of sleep

drinks.name: Black or green tea
drinks.notes: est.; 150 ml; between meals; polyphenols cut iron absorption near meals

drinks.name: Filter or instant coffee with milk
drinks.notes: est.; first 4 tea/coffee cups full, beyond 4 cups 50%; morning to early afternoon

drinks.name: Chaas (salted buttermilk)
drinks.notes: est.; 200 ml; with or after lunch or mid-afternoon; sodium about 170-400 mg (secondary, est.); Topic 18

drinks.name: Nimbu pani (homemade)
drinks.notes: est.; 250 ml; commute home or hot afternoon; reduce sugar and salt

drinks.name: Tender coconut water
drinks.notes: 200-250 ml; afternoon or after heat/exercise; potassium-rich (IFCT 2017 215 mg/100 g); kidney caution (Topic 19)

drinks.name: Milk, plain
drinks.notes: est.; 200 ml; breakfast or small bedtime amount; retains fluid longer (Maughan 2016)

drinks.name: Sweet lassi, packaged juice, sugarcane juice, soft drink
drinks.notes: est., product policy; free sugar over 8 g/100 ml; occasional

drinks.name: Herbal tea, caffeine-free
drinks.notes: est.; evening up to about 2 h before bed; check ingredients

drinks.name: ORS
drinks.notes: Illness only (diarrhoea, vomiting, heat illness); follow sachet label

drinks.name: Alcohol
drinks.notes: Not counted; raises urine output; disturbs sleep

reminderRules.rule: Maximum 6 reminders per day (7 on hot or workout days), at least 60 minutes apart

Current weekday app schedule 08:30, 10:30, 13:30, 16:00, 18:00 fits commuter and meal anchors; suggest adding or moving one reminder to about 12:45 for an optional pre-lunch glass, and starting the first reminder 30-60 minutes after the user's wake time
reminderRules.source: FitPlate design (est.); preload studies Davy 2008, Dennis 2010, Parretti 2016 (small effects)

reminderRules.rule: Skip a reminder if a drink of 150 ml or more was logged in the last 60 minutes; stop when the target is reached
Quiet hours default 21:00-08:00 on weekdays; last reminder at least 2-3 hours before the user's sleep time; night-shift users set quiet hours around their sleep
reminderRules.source: Swansea Bay NHS nocturia guidance (2 h before bed); Oelke 2017 review; FitPlate design (est.)

reminderRules.rule: Never prompt for more than about 500 ml at once; typical nudge 200-250 ml
reminderRules.source: Healthy kidney clears about 0.8-1.0 L/h at rest, less under stress (Verbalis via secondary summaries); Topic 35 (est.)

reminderRules.rule: No tea/coffee prompts within 1 hour of meals for users flagged iron-deficient; after 3 tea/coffee logs suggest water or chaas
reminderRules.source: ICMR-NIN 2024 (news summary, secondary, unverified); PubMed 10999016; Topic 21, 33

reminderRules.rule: Fasting mode (Ramadan, vrat): move reminders to allowed windows (iftar to suhoor); no reminders during fasting hours
reminderRules.source: Nutrients 2020 PRISMA review PMC7468808; Leiper and Molla 2003 (est.)

reminderRules.rule: Doctor-flag users (kidney disease, heart failure, diuretics, liver disease, fluid limit, nocturia or BPH on treatment, diabetes insipidus, pregnancy complications, uncontrolled diabetes): no automatic reminders or 'drink more' nudges; show 'Follow your doctor's fluid advice'

warnings: Evidence on the timing of water is thin; the schedule is a practical design (est.), not a proven protocol.
ICMR-NIN 2020 water values: Not found (primary). ICMR-NIN 2024 tea/coffee spacing is from news summaries (secondary, unverified).
Kidney, heart, liver disease, diuretics, nocturia/BPH, diabetes insipidus and pregnancy complications need doctor-set fluid timing (requires_doctor_input).
Do not drink more than about 500 ml at once; healthy kidneys clear about 0.8-1.0 L/h at rest and far less under stress; see Topic 35.
Waterless fasting in heat can cause dizziness and low blood pressure; people with medical conditions should ask a doctor.
Pre-meal water has small, uncertain effects on weight (Parretti 2016, Davy 2008; small non-Indian trials).
The Dubnov-Raz 2015 preload paper named in the brief could not be verified and is not used.
